en: This group-wide framework governs DOI allocation for journal content. Journals implement it prospectively through their published article-type, review and fee policies. Each journal identifies the sections it has adopted; eligibility is confirmed before publication. A DOI identifies a publication and does not certify peer review or guarantee indexing.

en: Approved complimentary sections charge no APC and may use Zenodo DOIs registered through DataCite. Eligible editorially reviewed content includes book, media and performance reviews; interviews and dialogues; conference reports; editorials and letters; translations and source texts; and creative works such as poetry, music and scores. Availability depends on the journal’s scope and published section policy. These works remain formal journal content and must meet its editorial, ethical, licensing and quality requirements.

en: Commentaries, perspectives, forums, review essays, critical reviews, translations and practice reflections require individual classification. Substantive externally peer-reviewed contributions normally use Crossref; approved complimentary content assessed through editorial review may use Zenodo. Routine news, calls for papers and administrative notices normally receive no DOI. Formal corrections, expressions of concern and retractions follow the relevant post-publication policy and are linked to the affected publication.

en: Existing DOIs are retained. When depositing the same published object in Zenodo, supply its existing DOI instead of generating a second one. Independently citable datasets, software or supplementary objects may have separate DOIs linked to the article. Exceptions require approval by the Editor-in-Chief or authorised Editorial Office and must preserve a clear scholarly record.

en: Zenodo deposits include the final published file, title, authors, ORCIDs where available, publication date, journal title, volume and issue, pages or article number, content type, licence and official journal article URL. The record and OJS publication page must link to each other; the assigned DOI is included on the article page and in the final file. Reserve a Zenodo DOI before finalising the file, and publish the deposit before describing the DOI as active. Clearly disclose editorial review or external peer review; DOI provider and APC status do not establish that distinction.

en:
Publication is the beginning of a work’s life in the scholarly record. We maintain the version of record, preserve accurate identifiers and metadata, and make important changes visible rather than silently replacing the original publication.

  • Minor errors may be corrected under the publication’s correction practice.
  • Material changes should have a separate correction, update, expression-of-concern, or retraction notice linked to the affected work.
  • Retractions are clearly identified and linked to the original record; a retracted work is not presented as an ordinary current publication.
  • Relevant DOI and discovery metadata should be updated so that the work’s status travels with its scholarly record.

Authors, readers, and reviewers may report a suspected error or integrity concern to the relevant journal or imprint. Reports are reviewed on their merits and may lead to a correction, clarification, investigation, or other appropriate action.

en:
Authors may appeal an editorial decision when they can identify a material procedural error, a significant misunderstanding of the work, or evidence that the applicable policy was not followed. An appeal should address the decision and should not simply restate the original submission.

Appeals are considered by the responsible editor or an independent editor designated for that purpose. A publication may decline to reopen a decision when no new material information is provided. The outcome is normally final for that submission.

Complaints about editorial conduct, peer review, authorship, or the handling of a published work should be submitted to the relevant editorial office. The publishing team can help route a question when the appropriate journal contact is unclear.

en:
Panorama Scholarly Group publishes research through journals, books, and related scholarly works. This standard sets shared expectations for editorial judgment, peer review, production, and post-publication stewardship across the group.

It applies to authors, editors, reviewers, editorial board members, production teams, and publishing staff. A journal or imprint may set more specific requirements for its field or format; those instructions should be read with this group-wide standard.

Er gilt für Autorinnen und Autoren, Redaktionen, Gutachtende, Beiratsmitglieder, Produktionsteams und Mitarbeitende im Verlagswesen. Eine Zeitschrift oder ein Imprint kann für sein Fachgebiet oder Format zusätzliche Anforderungen festlegen; diese sind zusammen mit dem gruppenweiten Standard zu lesen.

en:
Each publication describes its review model and decision pathway. Editors select reviewers with appropriate expertise and, where practicable, independence from the work and its authors.

  • Reviewers assess the work against the publication’s stated scope, criteria, and article or book type.
  • Manuscripts and reports remain confidential unless an open-review process has been announced.
  • Comments should address the work and its evidence, not the identity, institution, nationality, or personal circumstances of the authors.
  • Editors consider the full record and are not required to follow a reviewer’s recommendation.
  • Authors should receive a decision that clearly explains the principal grounds for the outcome.

A positive decision means that the work met the publication’s requirements at the time of assessment. It does not mean that the publisher or editors endorse every claim in the work.
old:
Jede Publikation beschreibt ihr Begutachtungsmodell und den Entscheidungsweg. Redaktionen wählen Gutachtende mit geeigneter Fachkompetenz und, soweit möglich, mit ausreichender Unabhängigkeit von Arbeit und Autorenschaft aus.

  • Gutachtende beurteilen die Arbeit anhand des veröffentlichten Umfangs, der Kriterien sowie der jeweiligen Artikel- oder Buchart.
  • Manuskripte und Gutachten bleiben vertraulich, sofern kein offenes Begutachtungsverfahren angekündigt wurde.
  • Kommentare sollen die Arbeit und ihre Nachweise betreffen, nicht Identität, Institution, Nationalität oder persönliche Umstände der Autorenschaft.
  • Redaktionen berücksichtigen die vollständige Aktenlage und müssen keiner einzelnen Empfehlung folgen.
  • Autorinnen und Autoren erhalten eine Entscheidung, aus der die wesentlichen Gründe hervorgehen.

Eine positive Entscheidung bedeutet, dass die Arbeit zum Zeitpunkt der Prüfung die Anforderungen der Publikation erfüllte. Sie bedeutet nicht, dass Verlag oder Redaktion jede Aussage der Arbeit billigen.

  • Redaktionen berücksichtigen die gesamte Aktenlage und sind nicht verpflichtet, der Empfehlung einer Gutachterin oder eines Gutachters zu folgen.
  • Autorinnen und Autoren erhalten eine Entscheidung, aus der die wesentlichen Gründe klar hervorgehen.

Eine positive Entscheidung bedeutet, dass die Arbeit zum Zeitpunkt der Prüfung die Anforderungen der Publikation erfüllte. Sie bedeutet nicht, dass Verlag oder Redaktion jede Aussage der Arbeit billigen.

en:
Authors must report their work honestly and with enough detail for readers to understand how conclusions were reached. Depending on the subject and method, this includes accurate descriptions of data, materials, methods, analysis, limitations, funding, approvals, and participant protections.

Panorama does not accept fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, duplicate or redundant publication, manipulated images, peer-review manipulation, or concealment of material conflicts. Concerns are assessed through appropriate editorial and research-integrity procedures, with confidentiality and due process respected as far as possible.

For allegations, complaints, misconduct, and publication-ethics procedures, see the Publication Ethics policy.
old:
Autorinnen und Autoren müssen ihre Arbeit wahrheitsgemäß und so ausführlich darstellen, dass die Herleitung der Schlussfolgerungen nachvollziehbar ist. Je nach Gegenstand und Methode umfasst dies genaue Angaben zu Daten, Materialien, Methoden, Analysen, Einschränkungen, Finanzierung, Genehmigungen und dem Schutz von Teilnehmenden.

Panorama akzeptiert keine Fälschung, Verfälschung, Plagiat, Doppel- oder redundante Veröffentlichung, manipulierte Abbildungen, Manipulation des Peer Review oder das Verschweigen wesentlicher Interessenkonflikte. Hinweise werden nach geeigneten redaktionellen und integritätsbezogenen Verfahren geprüft; Vertraulichkeit und ein faires Verfahren werden so weit wie möglich gewahrt.

Für Vorwürfe, Beschwerden, Fehlverhalten und Verfahren zur Publikationsethik siehe die Richtlinie zur Publikationsethik.

en:
Publication is the beginning of a work’s life in the scholarly record. We maintain the version of record, preserve accurate identifiers and metadata, and make important changes visible rather than silently replacing the original publication.

  • Minor errors may be corrected under the publication’s correction practice.
  • Material changes should have a separate correction, update, expression-of-concern, or retraction notice linked to the affected work.
  • Retractions are clearly identified and linked to the original record; a retracted work is not presented as an ordinary current publication.
  • Relevant DOI and discovery metadata should be updated so that the work’s status travels with its scholarly record.

Authors, readers, and reviewers may report a suspected error or integrity concern to the relevant journal or imprint. Reports are reviewed on their merits and may lead to a correction, clarification, investigation, or other appropriate action.
old:
Die Veröffentlichung ist der Beginn des Lebens einer Arbeit im wissenschaftlichen Record. Wir bewahren die Version of Record, erhalten korrekte Identifikatoren und Metadaten und machen wesentliche Änderungen sichtbar, statt die ursprüngliche Veröffentlichung stillschweigend zu ersetzen.

  • Geringfügige Fehler können nach dem Korrekturverfahren der Publikation berichtigt werden.
  • Wesentliche Änderungen erhalten eine eigene Korrektur-, Aktualisierungs-, Bedenken- oder Rücknahmebekanntmachung mit Verknüpfung zur betroffenen Arbeit.
  • Rücknahmen werden eindeutig gekennzeichnet und mit dem ursprünglichen Record verknüpft; eine zurückgenommene Arbeit wird nicht als gewöhnliche aktuelle Publikation dargestellt.
  • Relevante DOI- und Suchmetadaten werden aktualisiert, damit der Status der Arbeit mit ihrem wissenschaftlichen Record weitergegeben wird.

Autorenschaft, Leserschaft und Gutachtende können vermutete Fehler oder Integritätsbedenken der zuständigen Zeitschrift oder dem Imprint melden. Meldungen werden nach ihrem Inhalt geprüft und können zu einer Korrektur, Klarstellung, Untersuchung oder anderen geeigneten Maßnahme führen.
new:

Panorama may use more than one standard licence. The licence for a work is selected at journal, imprint, or agreement level and must be shown clearly on the work page, version-of-record file, and available metadata. The item-level notice is authoritative; readers should not infer a licence from the words “open access” alone.

  • CC BY 4.0. Sharing, adaptation, and commercial use are permitted with appropriate credit, a licence link, and an indication of changes.
  • CC BY-NC 4.0. Sharing and adaptation are permitted for non-commercial purposes with appropriate credit, a licence link, and an indication of changes.
  • CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Sharing is permitted for non-commercial purposes with appropriate credit, but adapted material may not be distributed under that licence.

A journal may specify another Creative Commons licence or bespoke rights arrangement only when it is stated in the governing agreement and on the published work. The official Creative Commons licence terms apply; this policy is not a substitute for the legal code.

Because these conditions differ, a non-commercial or no-derivatives licence may not satisfy every funder, repository, or indexer. Authors should check applicable requirements before accepting a licence.

en:
Authors are responsible for presenting their work accurately, completely, and in a form that allows readers to understand how conclusions were reached. Fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, duplicate publication, manipulated images, and deliberate concealment of material information are not acceptable.

  • Methods, data, materials, limitations, funding, approvals, and relevant use of tools must be reported accurately.
  • Questions about integrity may be referred to editors, institutions, funders, or other responsible bodies where appropriate.
  • Corrections, expressions of concern, and retractions are used when the evidence and applicable process require them.

Los autores son responsables de presentar su trabajo de forma exacta, completa y comprensible. No se aceptan la fabricación, falsificación, plagio, publicación duplicada, manipulación de imágenes ni ocultación deliberada de información relevante.

  • Los métodos, datos, materiales, limitaciones, financiación, aprobaciones y uso relevante de herramientas deben comunicarse con exactitud.
  • Las cuestiones de integridad pueden remitirse a editores, instituciones, financiadores u otros organismos responsables.
  • Se utilizan correcciones, expresiones de preocupación y retractaciones cuando las pruebas y el procedimiento aplicable lo exigen.

  • Los métodos, datos, materiales, limitaciones, financiación, aprobaciones y uso relevante de herramientas deben comunicarse con exactitud.
  • Las cuestiones de integridad pueden remitirse a editores, instituciones, financiadores u otros organismos responsables cuando proceda.

Authorship must reflect a substantial contribution to the work and responsibility for its content. All listed authors should approve the submission and be able to identify their contribution.

  • The corresponding author confirms that all authors have approved the submission and that no eligible contributor has been omitted.
  • Contributions, funding, professional assistance, and relevant tool use should be reported accurately.
  • Changes to authorship after submission or publication require a documented explanation and the agreement of affected authors, subject to editorial review.
  • Unresolved authorship matters may be referred to the relevant institution or employer.

en:
Each publication describes its review model and decision pathway. Editors select reviewers with appropriate expertise and, where practicable, independence from the work and its authors.

  • Reviewers assess the work against the publication’s stated scope, criteria, and article or book type.
  • Manuscripts and reports remain confidential unless an open-review process has been announced.
  • Comments should address the work and its evidence, not the identity, institution, nationality, or personal circumstances of the authors.
  • Editors consider the full record and are not required to follow a reviewer’s recommendation.
  • Authors should receive a decision that clearly explains the principal grounds for the outcome.

A positive decision means that the work met the publication’s requirements at the time of assessment. It does not mean that the publisher or editors endorse every claim in the work.

  • Les évaluateurs examinent le travail au regard du périmètre, des critères et du type d’article ou d’ouvrage annoncés.
  • Les manuscrits et rapports restent confidentiels, sauf annonce explicite d’une évaluation ouverte.
  • Les commentaires portent sur le travail et ses éléments probants, et non sur l’identité, l’établissement, la nationalité ou la situation personnelle des auteurs.
  • Les éditeurs examinent l’ensemble du dossier et ne sont pas tenus de suivre une recommandation particulière.
  • Les auteurs reçoivent une décision exposant clairement ses principaux motifs.

Une décision favorable signifie que le travail répondait aux exigences de la publication au moment de l’évaluation. Elle ne signifie pas que l’éditeur ou la revue approuve chacune de ses affirmations.

en:
Authors must report their work honestly and with enough detail for readers to understand how conclusions were reached. Depending on the subject and method, this includes accurate descriptions of data, materials, methods, analysis, limitations, funding, approvals, and participant protections.

Panorama does not accept fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, duplicate or redundant publication, manipulated images, peer-review manipulation, or concealment of material conflicts. Concerns are assessed through appropriate editorial and research-integrity procedures, with confidentiality and due process respected as far as possible.

For allegations, complaints, misconduct, and publication-ethics procedures, see the Publication Ethics policy.

en:
Publication is the beginning of a work’s life in the scholarly record. We maintain the version of record, preserve accurate identifiers and metadata, and make important changes visible rather than silently replacing the original publication.

  • Minor errors may be corrected under the publication’s correction practice.
  • Material changes should have a separate correction, update, expression-of-concern, or retraction notice linked to the affected work.
  • Retractions are clearly identified and linked to the original record; a retracted work is not presented as an ordinary current publication.
  • Relevant DOI and discovery metadata should be updated so that the work’s status travels with its scholarly record.

Authors, readers, and reviewers may report a suspected error or integrity concern to the relevant journal or imprint. Reports are reviewed on their merits and may lead to a correction, clarification, investigation, or other appropriate action.

  • Les erreurs mineures peuvent être corrigées selon la procédure de la publication.
  • Les changements importants doivent faire l’objet d’un avis distinct de correction, de mise à jour, d’expression de préoccupation ou de rétractation, lié au travail concerné.
  • Les rétractations sont clairement signalées et liées au dossier initial ; un travail rétracté n’est pas présenté comme une publication courante ordinaire.
  • Les métadonnées DOI et de découverte pertinentes sont mises à jour afin que le statut du travail accompagne son dossier scientifique.

Les auteurs, lecteurs et évaluateurs peuvent signaler une erreur présumée ou une question d’intégrité à la revue ou à la marque éditoriale concernée. Les signalements sont examinés sur le fond et peuvent conduire à une correction, une clarification, une enquête ou toute autre mesure appropriée.

Panorama may use more than one standard licence. The licence for a work is selected at journal, imprint, or agreement level and must be shown clearly on the work page, version-of-record file, and available metadata. The item-level notice is authoritative; readers should not infer a licence from the words “open access” alone.

  • CC BY 4.0. Sharing, adaptation, and commercial use are permitted with appropriate credit, a licence link, and an indication of changes.
  • CC BY-NC 4.0. Sharing and adaptation are permitted for non-commercial purposes with appropriate credit, a licence link, and an indication of changes.
  • CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Sharing is permitted for non-commercial purposes with appropriate credit, but adapted material may not be distributed under that licence.

A journal may specify another Creative Commons licence or bespoke rights arrangement only when it is stated in the governing agreement and on the published work. The official Creative Commons licence terms apply; this policy is not a substitute for the legal code.

Because these conditions differ, a non-commercial or no-derivatives licence may not satisfy every funder, repository, or indexer. Authors should check applicable requirements before accepting a licence.

en:
Authors may appeal an editorial decision when they can identify a material procedural error, a significant misunderstanding of the work, or evidence that the applicable policy was not followed. An appeal should address the decision and should not simply restate the original submission.

Appeals are considered by the responsible editor or an independent editor designated for that purpose. A publication may decline to reopen a decision when no new material information is provided. The outcome is normally final for that submission.

Complaints about editorial conduct, peer review, authorship, or the handling of a published work should be submitted to the relevant editorial office. The publishing team can help route a question when the appropriate journal contact is unclear.

en:
We accept credible concerns about research integrity, authorship, conflicts, peer review, editorial conduct, permissions, or the accuracy of a published work. Reports should contain enough information for the responsible team to understand the concern and identify supporting evidence.

  • Reports are handled as confidentially as circumstances allow, while preserving a fair opportunity to respond.
  • We may request documents, consult responsible bodies, and pause editorial action while facts are established.
  • We do not make findings based on identity, nationality, affiliation, status, or disagreement with a lawful scholarly position.
  • Good-faith reporting is not grounds for retaliation; deliberately false or abusive reports may be treated separately.

A publication may reject, withdraw, correct, annotate, or refer a work when the evidence and process support that action.

en:
Panorama may use more than one standard licence. The licence for a work is selected at journal, imprint, or agreement level and must be shown clearly on the work page, version-of-record file, and available metadata. The item-level notice is authoritative; readers should not infer a licence from the words “open access” alone.

  • CC BY 4.0. Sharing, adaptation, and commercial use are permitted with appropriate credit, a licence link, and an indication of changes.
  • CC BY-NC 4.0. Sharing and adaptation are permitted for non-commercial purposes with appropriate credit, a licence link, and an indication of changes.
  • CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Sharing is permitted for non-commercial purposes with appropriate credit, but adapted material may not be distributed under that licence.

A journal may specify another Creative Commons licence or bespoke rights arrangement only when it is stated in the governing agreement and on the published work. The official Creative Commons licence terms apply; this policy is not a substitute for the legal code.

Because these conditions differ, a non-commercial or no-derivatives licence may not satisfy every funder, repository, or indexer. Authors should check applicable requirements before accepting a licence.

  • CC BY 4.0. 적절한 출처 표시, 라이선스 링크 및 변경 표시를 조건으로 공유, 변경 및 상업적 이용을 허용합니다.
  • CC BY-NC 4.0. 적절한 출처 표시, 링크 및 변경 표시를 조건으로 비영리 목적의 공유와 변경을 허용합니다.
  • CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. 적절한 출처 표시를 조건으로 비영리 목적의 공유를 허용하지만 변경된 자료의 배포는 허용하지 않습니다.

다른 크리에이티브 커먼즈 라이선스나 개별 권리 조건은 적용 계약과 출판물에 명시된 경우에만 지정할 수 있습니다. 해당 라이선스의 공식 조건이 적용되며 본 정책은 법률 문안을 대체하지 않습니다.

학술지는 다른 크리에이티브 커먼즈 라이선스나 개별 권리 조건을 적용 계약과 출판물에 명시된 경우에만 지정할 수 있습니다. 공식 크리에이티브 커먼즈 라이선스 조건이 적용되며 본 정책은 법률 문안을 대체하지 않습니다.

en:
Article processing charges, book publication charges, colour or supplementary-material charges, waivers, discounts, and other fees are publication-specific. Any applicable charge and its basis should be disclosed before acceptance. A fee is not payment for acceptance, and ability to pay must not determine scholarly merit.

en:
We preserve the version of record and maintain the relationship between the work, its DOI, its licence, and post-publication notices. Corrections, updates, expressions of concern, and retractions are linked to the affected work and identified clearly in the work page and metadata.

Retractions remain visible. A work marked Retracted must not be presented as a current reliable publication. A licence does not authorise removal of a retraction notice or misrepresentation of the work’s status.

A correction or retraction notice may itself contain separate rights or privacy restrictions. Readers should use the linked notice and current version-of-record status when citing or reusing a work.

en: Commentaries, perspectives, forums, review essays, critical reviews, translations and practice reflections require individual classification. Substantive externally peer-reviewed contributions normally use Crossref; approved complimentary content assessed through editorial review may use Zenodo. Routine news, calls for papers and administrative notices normally receive no DOI. Formal corrections, expressions of concern and retractions follow the relevant post-publication policy and are linked to the affected publication.
old: Комментарии, перспективы, форумы, обзорные эссе, критические обзоры, переводы и размышления о практике классифицируются индивидуально. Содержательные внешне рецензируемые работы обычно используют Crossref; утверждённые бесплатные материалы с редакционной проверкой могут использовать Zenodo. Обычные новости, приглашения к публикации и административные объявления обычно не получают DOI. Формальные исправления, выражения обеспокоенности и ретракции регулируются соответствующей политикой и связаны с затронутой публикацией.
new: Комментарии, авторские точки зрения, форумы, обзорные эссе, критические обзоры, переводы и размышления о практике классифицируются индивидуально. Содержательные работы, прошедшие внешнее рецензирование, обычно получают DOI Crossref; утверждённые бесплатные материалы, прошедшие редакционную проверку, могут получать DOI Zenodo. Обычные новости, приглашения к подаче статей и административные объявления, как правило, не получают DOI. Официальные исправления, выражения обеспокоенности и ретракции оформляются в соответствии с политикой в отношении опубликованных материалов и связываются с затронутой публикацией.
reason: 'перспективы' is a calque for the article type; 'post-publication' policy was omitted; awkward 'внешне рецензируемые'.

en: Zenodo deposits include the final published file, title, authors, ORCIDs where available, publication date, journal title, volume and issue, pages or article number, content type, licence and official journal article URL. The record and OJS publication page must link to each other; the assigned DOI is included on the article page and in the final file. Reserve a Zenodo DOI before finalising the file, and publish the deposit before describing the DOI as active. Clearly disclose editorial review or external peer review; DOI provider and APC status do not establish that distinction.
old: Запись Zenodo включает окончательный файл, название, авторов, доступные ORCID, дату, журнал, том, выпуск, страницы или номер статьи, тип, лицензию и официальный URL. Репозиторий и страница OJS взаимно связаны; DOI указан на странице и в окончательном файле. DOI резервируют до завершения файла и называют активным только после публикации записи. Редакционная проверка и внешнее рецензирование обозначаются явно; провайдер DOI и статус APC не заменяют эту информацию.
new: Запись в Zenodo включает окончательный опубликованный файл, название, авторов, идентификаторы ORCID (при наличии), дату публикации, название журнала, том и выпуск, страницы или номер статьи, тип материала, лицензию и официальный URL статьи на сайте журнала. Запись и страница публикации в OJS должны содержать взаимные ссылки; присвоенный DOI указывается на странице статьи и в окончательном файле. DOI Zenodo резервируют до окончательной подготовки файла, а называть DOI активным можно только после публикации записи. Необходимо чётко указывать, прошла ли работа редакционную проверку или внешнее рецензирование: провайдер DOI и статус APC не определяют это различие.

en:
Each publication describes its review model and decision pathway. Editors select reviewers with appropriate expertise and, where practicable, independence from the work and its authors.

  • Reviewers assess the work against the publication’s stated scope, criteria, and article or book type.
  • Manuscripts and reports remain confidential unless an open-review process has been announced.
  • Comments should address the work and its evidence, not the identity, institution, nationality, or personal circumstances of the authors.
  • Editors consider the full record and are not required to follow a reviewer’s recommendation.
  • Authors should receive a decision that clearly explains the principal grounds for the outcome.

A positive decision means that the work met the publication’s requirements at the time of assessment. It does not mean that the publisher or editors endorse every claim in the work.

en:
Authors must report their work honestly and with enough detail for readers to understand how conclusions were reached. Depending on the subject and method, this includes accurate descriptions of data, materials, methods, analysis, limitations, funding, approvals, and participant protections.

Panorama does not accept fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, duplicate or redundant publication, manipulated images, peer-review manipulation, or concealment of material conflicts. Concerns are assessed through appropriate editorial and research-integrity procedures, with confidentiality and due process respected as far as possible.

For allegations, complaints, misconduct, and publication-ethics procedures, see the Publication Ethics policy.

en:
Publication is the beginning of a work’s life in the scholarly record. We maintain the version of record, preserve accurate identifiers and metadata, and make important changes visible rather than silently replacing the original publication.

  • Minor errors may be corrected under the publication’s correction practice.
  • Material changes should have a separate correction, update, expression-of-concern, or retraction notice linked to the affected work.
  • Retractions are clearly identified and linked to the original record; a retracted work is not presented as an ordinary current publication.
  • Relevant DOI and discovery metadata should be updated so that the work’s status travels with its scholarly record.

Authors, readers, and reviewers may report a suspected error or integrity concern to the relevant journal or imprint. Reports are reviewed on their merits and may lead to a correction, clarification, investigation, or other appropriate action.

  • Незначительные ошибки могут исправляться по процедуре соответствующего издания.
  • Существенные изменения должны сопровождаться отдельным уведомлением об исправлении, обновлении, заявлении о сомнениях или отзыве, связанным с затронутой работой.
  • Отозванные работы ясно обозначаются и связываются с исходной записью; они не представляются как обычные действующие публикации.
  • Соответствующие DOI и метаданные поиска обновляются, чтобы статус работы сохранялся во всей научной записи.

Авторы, читатели и рецензенты могут сообщить о предполагаемой ошибке или проблеме добросовестности соответствующему журналу или издательскому бренду. Сообщения рассматриваются по существу и могут привести к исправлению, разъяснению, расследованию или иной мере.

en:
Each publication describes its review model and decision pathway. Editors select reviewers with appropriate expertise and, where practicable, independence from the work and its authors.

  • Reviewers assess the work against the publication’s stated scope, criteria, and article or book type.
  • Manuscripts and reports remain confidential unless an open-review process has been announced.
  • Comments should address the work and its evidence, not the identity, institution, nationality, or personal circumstances of the authors.
  • Editors consider the full record and are not required to follow a reviewer’s recommendation.
  • Authors should receive a decision that clearly explains the principal grounds for the outcome.

A positive decision means that the work met the publication’s requirements at the time of assessment. It does not mean that the publisher or editors endorse every claim in the work.

  • 审稿人应依据出版物公开的范围、标准及文章或图书类型评审成果。
  • 除非已明确采用开放式评审，稿件及评审报告应予保密。
  • 评审意见应针对成果及其证据，不得针对作者的身份、机构、国籍或个人情况。
  • 编辑应综合全部材料作出判断，不必机械采纳任何单一审稿意见。

en:
Authors may appeal an editorial decision when they can identify a material procedural error, a significant misunderstanding of the work, or evidence that the applicable policy was not followed. An appeal should address the decision and should not simply restate the original submission.

Appeals are considered by the responsible editor or an independent editor designated for that purpose. A publication may decline to reopen a decision when no new material information is provided. The outcome is normally final for that submission.

Complaints about editorial conduct, peer review, authorship, or the handling of a published work should be submitted to the relevant editorial office. The publishing team can help route a question when the appropriate journal contact is unclear.

en:
We accept credible concerns about research integrity, authorship, conflicts, peer review, editorial conduct, permissions, or the accuracy of a published work. Reports should contain enough information for the responsible team to understand the concern and identify supporting evidence.

  • Reports are handled as confidentially as circumstances allow, while preserving a fair opportunity to respond.
  • We may request documents, consult responsible bodies, and pause editorial action while facts are established.
  • We do not make findings based on identity, nationality, affiliation, status, or disagreement with a lawful scholarly position.
  • Good-faith reporting is not grounds for retaliation; deliberately false or abusive reports may be treated separately.

A publication may reject, withdraw, correct, annotate, or refer a work when the evidence and process support that action.

en:
We preserve the version of record and make material changes visible. A material error, unresolved concern, or unreliable result may require a correction, clarification, expression of concern, or retraction.

A retraction notice should be clearly labelled, linked to the affected work, freely available, and published promptly. The original record is not silently erased except for legal, safety, privacy, or other exceptional reasons, and retraction status should be carried through relevant DOI, indexing, and discovery metadata.

Important: A work marked Retracted is not treated as a current reliable publication. Readers should follow the retraction notice and use the corrected or replacement record where one exists.

en:
Each publication describes its review model and decision pathway. Editors select reviewers with appropriate expertise and, where practicable, independence from the work and its authors.

  • Reviewers assess the work against the publication’s stated scope, criteria, and article or book type.
  • Manuscripts and reports remain confidential unless an open-review process has been announced.
  • Comments should address the work and its evidence, not the identity, institution, nationality, or personal circumstances of the authors.
  • Editors consider the full record and are not required to follow a reviewer’s recommendation.
  • Authors should receive a decision that clearly explains the principal grounds for the outcome.

A positive decision means that the work met the publication’s requirements at the time of assessment. It does not mean that the publisher or editors endorse every claim in the work.

en:
Publication is the beginning of a work’s life in the scholarly record. We maintain the version of record, preserve accurate identifiers and metadata, and make important changes visible rather than silently replacing the original publication.

  • Minor errors may be corrected under the publication’s correction practice.
  • Material changes should have a separate correction, update, expression-of-concern, or retraction notice linked to the affected work.
  • Retractions are clearly identified and linked to the original record; a retracted work is not presented as an ordinary current publication.
  • Relevant DOI and discovery metadata should be updated so that the work’s status travels with its scholarly record.

Authors, readers, and reviewers may report a suspected error or integrity concern to the relevant journal or imprint. Reports are reviewed on their merits and may lead to a correction, clarification, investigation, or other appropriate action.

en:
Each publication describes its review model and decision pathway. Editors select reviewers with appropriate expertise and, where practicable, independence from the work and its authors.

  • Reviewers assess the work against the publication’s stated scope, criteria, and article or book type.
  • Manuscripts and reports remain confidential unless an open-review process has been announced.
  • Comments should address the work and its evidence, not the identity, institution, nationality, or personal circumstances of the authors.
  • Editors consider the full record and are not required to follow a reviewer’s recommendation.
  • Authors should receive a decision that clearly explains the principal grounds for the outcome.

A positive decision means that the work met the publication’s requirements at the time of assessment. It does not mean that the publisher or editors endorse every claim in the work.
old:
Chaque publication décrit son modèle d’évaluation et son circuit de décision. Les éditeurs choisissent des évaluateurs disposant de l’expertise requise et, lorsque cela est possible, indépendants du travail et de ses auteurs.

  • Les évaluateurs examinent le travail au regard du périmètre, des critères et du type d’article ou d’ouvrage annoncés.
  • Les manuscrits et rapports restent confidentiels, sauf annonce explicite d’une évaluation ouverte.
  • Les commentaires portent sur le travail et ses éléments probants, et non sur l’identité, l’établissement, la nationalité ou la situation personnelle des auteurs.
  • Les éditeurs examinent l’ensemble du dossier et ne sont pas tenus de suivre la recommandation d’un évaluateur.
  • Les auteurs reçoivent une décision exposant clairement ses principaux motifs.

Une décision favorable signifie que le travail répondait aux exigences de la publication au moment de l’évaluation. Elle ne signifie pas que la maison d’édition ou les éditeurs approuvent chacune de ses affirmations.

en:
Publication is the beginning of a work’s life in the scholarly record. We maintain the version of record, preserve accurate identifiers and metadata, and make important changes visible rather than silently replacing the original publication.

  • Minor errors may be corrected under the publication’s correction practice.
  • Material changes should have a separate correction, update, expression-of-concern, or retraction notice linked to the affected work.
  • Retractions are clearly identified and linked to the original record; a retracted work is not presented as an ordinary current publication.
  • Relevant DOI and discovery metadata should be updated so that the work’s status travels with its scholarly record.

Authors, readers, and reviewers may report a suspected error or integrity concern to the relevant journal or imprint. Reports are reviewed on their merits and may lead to a correction, clarification, investigation, or other appropriate action.

  • Les erreurs mineures peuvent être corrigées selon les pratiques de correction de la publication.
  • Les changements importants doivent faire l’objet d’un avis distinct de correction, de mise à jour, d’expression de préoccupation ou de rétractation, lié au travail concerné.
  • Les rétractations sont clairement signalées et liées au dossier initial ; un travail rétracté n’est pas présenté comme une publication courante ordinaire.
  • Les métadonnées DOI et de découverte pertinentes sont mises à jour afin que le statut du travail accompagne son dossier scientifique.

Les auteurs, lecteurs et évaluateurs peuvent signaler une erreur présumée ou une question d’intégrité à la revue ou à la marque éditoriale concernée. Les signalements sont examinés sur le fond et peuvent conduire à une correction, une clarification, une enquête ou toute autre mesure appropriée.

en:
Authors may appeal an editorial decision when they can identify a material procedural error, a significant misunderstanding of the work, or evidence that the applicable policy was not followed. An appeal should address the decision and should not simply restate the original submission.

Appeals are considered by the responsible editor or an independent editor designated for that purpose. A publication may decline to reopen a decision when no new material information is provided. The outcome is normally final for that submission.

Complaints about editorial conduct, peer review, authorship, or the handling of a published work should be submitted to the relevant editorial office. The publishing team can help route a question when the appropriate journal contact is unclear.

Les auteurs indiquent l’organisme compétent ou expliquent pourquoi aucun examen formel n’était requis et décrivent, le cas échéant, consentement, vie privée, confidentialité, enregistrement et protection des participants.

Les éditeurs peuvent demander des preuves d’autorisation, de consentement, d’enregistrement, de gouvernance des données ou de droits. La publication peut être suspendue pendant l’évaluation d’un risque immédiat ou grave.

en:
Authors may appeal an editorial decision when they can identify a material procedural error, a significant misunderstanding of the work, or evidence that the applicable policy was not followed. An appeal should address the stated grounds and should not simply repeat the original submission.

Appeals are considered by the responsible editor or an independent editor designated for that purpose. An appeal may be declined when it provides no material new information. Post-publication questions are considered on their merits and may lead to an appropriate notice.
old:
Les auteurs peuvent contester une décision éditoriale s’ils identifient une erreur de procédure importante, une incompréhension substantielle ou le non-respect de la politique applicable. Le recours doit répondre aux motifs indiqués et ne pas répéter la soumission initiale.

Les recours sont examinés par l’éditeur responsable ou un éditeur indépendant désigné. Ils peuvent être refusés sans information nouvelle substantielle. Les questions post-publication sont examinées sur le fond et peuvent donner lieu à un avis approprié.

en:
Panorama Scholarly Group supports editors in applying publication criteria, maintaining editorial independence, protecting confidential information, preserving the version of record, and responding to credible concerns. We maintain public policies and reliable metadata so readers can understand the status and provenance of published work.

This policy is a group-wide framework, not an exhaustive code for every discipline or situation. Questions or complaints can be sent to the relevant editorial office or through the group contact page when the appropriate destination is unclear.

en: Commentaries, perspectives, forums, review essays, critical reviews, translations and practice reflections require individual classification. Formal corrections, expressions of concern and retractions follow the relevant post-publication policy and are linked to the affected publication.
